steps.name: Paired DESeq2 differential expression (control vs treated, subject-blocked)
caveats: With only 5 subjects, the paired design has 4 residual degrees of freedom for the condition effect after accounting for subject — power is limited; report this explicitly rather than overclaiming
Confirm the metadata subject/condition columns match the exact column headers used to order counts.csv samples before fitting the design formula
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control blood samples across the 5 paired subjects, controlling for subject-to-subject variability (design ~subject + condition)?
constraints: Do not drop the subject blocking term from the design — an unpaired ~condition model would ignore the paired structure explicit in the data context and inflate false positives/negatives
Use raw integer counts as-is; do not pre-normalize before DESeq2 (it performs its own size-factor normalization)
acceptance_criteria: Counts (12000 genes x 10 samples) and metadata (10 rows: subject, condition) are loaded and joined; sample order in counts matches metadata rows exactly
Genes with near-zero counts across all samples are filtered before modeling (e.g. rowSum or rowMean count filter)
DESeq2 is run with design ~subject + condition (paired/blocked design), condition releveled so control is the reference
Output table includes log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC (apeglm or ashr), p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value per gene, ranked by adjusted p-value
A results table (CSV) and summary counts of significant genes (padj < 0.05) are saved for downstream steps

steps.name: Per-subject treated-vs-control fold-change and concordance
caveats: Single-pair-per-subject fold-changes are noisy point estimates, not statistically tested effects — do not present them as subject-level significant DE calls
Use DESeq2 size factors from T1S1 (not raw counts) to normalize per-subject fold-changes for library size differences
steps.question: For each of the 5 subjects individually, what is the treated-vs-control log2 fold-change per gene, and how concordant are these subject-level responses across subjects — i.e., which genes respond consistently within each subject versus which respond heterogeneously?
constraints: Do not compute or report a p-value per subject per gene from a single paired sample — there is no replication to support one
acceptance_criteria: For each of the 5 subjects, a simple paired log2((treated+pseudocount)/(control+pseudocount)) or size-factor-normalized fold-change is computed per gene using that subject's own control/treated pair
A subject x gene fold-change matrix (5 rows, genes as columns or long-format table) is produced covering all filtered genes

For the genes flagged significant in the paired DESeq2 model (T1S1), report per-subject fold-change values, sign concordance (fraction of the 5 subjects showing the same direction of change) and a concordance score (e.g. mean pairwise correlation of per-subject LFCs, or fraction of subjects with |LFC|>threshold in the same direction)

Explicitly states that per-subject significance testing is not performed (each subject contributes a single pair, i.e., no within-subject replication for a per-subject p-value) — only descriptive fold-change and concordance are reported
Output includes a table of top concordant treatment-responsive genes and a table/plot of genes with discordant (subject-specific) responses

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: WikiPathways human gene sets use HGNC gene symbols — confirm counts.csv gene identifiers are also HGNC symbols (per data context, first column is gene symbol) before matching
With only 12000 genes profiled, some larger pathways may have low background coverage; note this as a limitation of interpretation
steps.question: Which WikiPathways biological pathways are enriched among the genes significantly differentially expressed between control and treated blood samples (from the paired DESeq2 model)?
constraints: Use only the human (Homo sapiens) WikiPathways gene set file — do not substitute the mouse or rat WikiPathways files present in the reference store
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g. over-representation or fgsea pre-ranked on the DESeq2 stat/LFC) is run against the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the reference store
If the WikiPathways human GMT reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports this explicitly and skips enrichment rather than fabricating results
Significant genes (padj < 0.05) from T1S1 are used as the query/ranked gene list, matched by gene symbol
Output is a ranked table of enriched pathways with p-value, adjusted p-value (BH/FDR), and leading-edge/overlapping genes per pathway
Report gene symbol mapping rate against pathway gene sets (fraction of input genes matched) so silent identifier mismatches are visible

plan.title: Paired control vs treated DE analysis in blood (n=5)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (STAR/featureCounts raw integer counts, 12000 genes x 11 columns i.e. gene symbol + 10 samples) from 5 human blood subjects, each contributing a paired control and treated sample. This paired design lets us isolate the treatment effect while controlling for inter-subject variability by including subject as a blocking factor in a paired differential expression model. Step 1 loads counts and metadata, verifies the pairing (5 subjects x 2 conditions = 10 samples matches the 11-column count file: 1 gene-symbol column + 10 sample columns), filters low-count genes, and runs DESeq2 with a paired design (~subject + condition) to get one genome-wide list of genes that respond to treatment across subjects (accounting for the paired structure), which directly answers 'which genes respond to treatment' in an aggregate, subject-controlled sense. Step 2 additionally computes each subject's individual treated-vs-control log2 fold-changes (paired per-subject contrasts) to characterize which genes respond 'within each subject' as literally asked - reporting per-subject fold-changes/concordance across the 5 pairs, since the sample size does not support formal per-subject significance testing (n=1 pair per subject) but does support consistency/concordance analysis (e.g., sign consistency, correlation of subject-level shrunken LFCs from Step 1's paired model vs. genes computed subject-by-subject). Step 3 takes the significant paired-DESeq2 gene list and performs pathway enrichment using the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the reference store, to give biological interpretation of the treatment-responsive genes.
